name: Wounded Warrior Project (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: Wounded Warrior Project's programmes for post-9/11 veterans in the US (mental health has its own model).
summary: Wounded Warrior Project serves post-9/11 veterans injured in service and their families in the United States: it wins VA disability benefits for them, places them in jobs, gives emergency grants and financial counselling, runs social and fitness events, pays for in-home care for the most severely injured, funds other veteran charities and lobbies Congress. Our model of every programme but mental health in fiscal 2025 ($175.9M of $274.6M programme spending; mental health is wounded-warrior-project-charityevals-mental-health) values the benefits won, jobs, grants and care on the site's log-income scale, the benefits net of what they cost taxpayers, the events by life satisfaction, and the Major Richard Star Act's chance of passing; it comes to about 0.006 years of healthy life per $1,000, low because the help goes to US households that already consume about $27,000 a person, and most VA awards it helps win would have come through another free representative or later. About four-fifths of the result is the benefits service ($263.7M of awards in WWP's own unexplained 'economic impact' figure), net of what the awards cost taxpayers, with credit shared with the VA's own cost of deciding the claims. Every branch but the emergency grants is discounted for missing data: benefits, Warriors to Work, financial readiness, connection, physical health, the Independence Program, community partnerships and advocacy. The biggest uncertainties are how many years of payments an award adds over what veterans would have won anyway and how far below average the veterans' consumption is; with every judgment at its ends the result spans over a thousandfold, so it is mostly uncertainty.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

Benefits service: 'economic impact' of the VA awards won, fiscal 2025

source.title: Wounded Warrior Project, Form 990 for the year ended 30 September 2025
source.quote: IN FISCAL YEAR 2025, ISSUES AWARDED ON BEHALF OF WARRIORS THROUGH BENEFITS SERVICE RESULTED IN AN ECONOMIC IMPACT OF $263.7 MILLION.

rows.explainer: WWP's VA-accredited representatives file and argue disability compensation claims for veterans. The figure is WWP's own and its method isn't published; how many years of payments it stands for is ben_years_in_figure.

rows.label: Years of added payments WWP's figure stands for
rows.explainer: WWP doesn't say. Its 2016 release spoke of 'annualized monetary benefits', and its 2015 release of 'annual and retroactive benefits'; so the figure is most likely a year of the added monthly payments plus some back pay for claims decided in the year. A 10% rating pays about $2,100 a year and each step up roughly $2,000 to $4,000 more. 1.2 (0.8-2).

rows.label: People per household
rows.explainer: The site's US figure (2.4 per consumer unit): grants, awards and wages are household income.

rows.label: Cost per person reached (all branches, people counted once per branch)
rows.formula: cost_total / (people_reached + ben_people + emp_placed * household_size + finr_people * household_size + ind_warriors * household_size + cp_households * household_size + con_alumni + phys_participants)
rows.explainer: Context: the six programmes' cost over everyone they reach, counting a household's members and each branch once (people in several branches are counted in each).

Average consumption per person in the US, fiscal-2025 dollars (US$)
rows.explainer: The site's survey figure (Consumer Expenditure Survey, $32,723 a person in 2024), put into 2025 prices by the US consumer price index (Convention 8).

rows.label: Veterans' households helped to an award in the year
rows.explainer: Not reported. Judgment: the $263.7M at about $13,000 of added payments a household-year (a rise of two or three rating steps, or a first rating of 30-50%, plus back pay) over 1.2 years is about 17,000 veterans; 8,000 if awards are larger, 35,000 if most are single small increases. One veteran per household.

rows.label: People in the households helped to an award
Added VA payments per person in a household helped, per year (US$)
rows.explainer: About $5,400 a person a year at the best guesses ($12,900 a household), spread over the household as household income.

rows.label: Consumption per person of the veterans' households helped to an award, as a share of the average
rows.explainer: Anchors: the poorest fifth spends 0.45 of the average household (@united_states.ce_lowest_quintile_vs_all_2024), the second fifth 0.64. Post-9/11 veterans with service-connected injuries mostly work or draw military retirement or VA pay, but WWP's own survey finds 67% of its warriors had 'not enough money in the past 12 months' and 75% call their debts somewhat or very unmanageable (annual report p. 14). 0.8 of the average (0.5-1.1).

rows.label: Consumption per person of the households helped (US$)
Years of added payments an award brings, averaged over the awards WWP's help changes
rows.explainer: Service-connected ratings are rarely reduced and are paid for life: a 40-year-old US man expects about 38 more years (Social Security period life table), about 20 years discounted at the shared rate. But most awards WWP's help changes would have come later anyway, through another representative, a supplemental claim (decided in about four to five months) or an appeal to the Board (years); for those the gain is the months or years brought forward. 10 years (3-25) averaged over both, discounted below; whether an award would have come at the same time without WWP is ben_counterfactual_adj.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person, benefits branch, discounted
rows.explainer: The site's one log-income scale at the veterans' own consumption, over the years the payments run, discounted.

rows.label: Marginal cost of public funds
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure (facts/public_funds.json): 1.2, range 1 (money shifted from other spending) to 1.5.

rows.label: How US federal taxes fall, relative to a tax proportional to consumption
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure (facts/public_funds.json): VA compensation and military retirement pay are federal money, paid by the federal income tax and borrowing, which fall mostly on richer households: 1.4 (1-2).

rows.label: Log-consumption loss to taxpayers per dollar of benefits paid
rows.explainer: VA compensation is paid from federal revenue, spread thinly over many payers: each dollar costs the marginal cost of public funds over the payers' consumption (the survey mean the veterans are measured on, docs/normalization.md 2.14).

rows.label: Share of the financial wellness line spent on the benefits service
rows.explainer: The line pays for the benefits team (VA-accredited representatives in WWP's 27 offices), Warriors to Work's career coaches (62,460 coaching services) and financial readiness, plus $3.7M of emergency grants. No split is published; about half (0.3-0.7) by the staff the services need.

rows.label: VA's cost of deciding a disability claim (US$)
rows.explainer: The Veterans Benefits Administration's General Operating Expenses account was $3,899M in 2025 (VA 2026 Budget in Brief) and it completed 3,001,734 disability compensation and pension claims in fiscal 2025 (VA's figure, reported by GovCIO): about $1,300 a claim. Part of the account pays for education, home loans and other benefits, so a disability claim's share is lower: $1,000 (700-1,400), the government staff time behind each award (Convention 2). Sources: https://department.va.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/2026-Budget-in-Brief.pdf ; https://govciomedia.com/va-uses-automation-ai-to-process-record-benefits-claims/

source.title: US Department of Veterans Affairs (June 2025), 2026 Budget in Brief (General Operating Expenses, Veterans Benefits Administration)
source.quote: General Operating Expenses, Veterans Benefits Administration 3,869 3,899 3,879

rows.label: WWP's share of the resources behind the awards it changes
rows.formula: fin_spend * ben_team_share * overhead_ratio / (fin_spend * ben_team_share * overhead_ratio + vba_cost_per_claim * ben_households * ben_counterfactual_adj)
rows.explainer: WWP's cost of the benefits service against the VA's cost of deciding the claims whose award WWP changes: about 0.8 at the best guesses.

rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights for the veterans' age bands, times your value of a life; read by the connection branch's suicides averted.

rows.explainer: Pay less income and payroll taxes (about a fifth at these earnings) and less what the household had before the job: unemployment pay, a partner's extra work, VA unemployability pay or a lower-paid job, which for people placed through a careers programme is often substantial. 0.5 (0.3-0.7).

rows.label: Years the job gain lasts against finding work without WWP
rows.explainer: Job-search help mostly speeds up finding work: in Card, Kluve and Weber's meta-analysis of 207 evaluations of active labour market programmes (2018, Journal of the European Economic Association 16:894), job search assistance has its effect in the first year after the programme and little after two. 1 year (0.5-3).

rows.formula: ln(1 + emp_annual_pay / emp_placed * emp_net_share / household_size / (consumption_mean * emp_consumption_share)) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, emp_years)

source.title: Wounded Warrior Project, Form 990 for the year ended 30 September 2025
source.quote: THE PEER SUPPORT PROGRAM SERVED 12,705 WARRIORS AT PEER FACILITATED SUPPORT GROUPS IN FISCAL YEAR 2025.

rows.explainer: Small warrior-only groups led by volunteer peers, 1,300 meetings in the year. Mostly also at alumni events: their gain here is on top.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained from alumni events while it lasts (points, 0-10)
rows.explainer: A few social events a year for isolated veterans (79% of WWP warriors report feeling isolated). Anchor: the Salvation Army model's community programmes (0.03, 0.005-0.1); loneliness interventions average about 0.2 SD on loneliness (Masi et al. 2011, Personality and Social Psychology Review 15:219), and an occasional event is far less than those programmes.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained from peer support groups while it lasts (points, 0-10)
rows.explainer: Regular warrior-only groups: closer to the loneliness and peer-support trials (Masi et al. 2011, about 0.2 SD on loneliness; Pfeiffer et al. 2011, peer support for depression), which is roughly 0.1 to 0.4 life-satisfaction points at 2 points per SD, scaled down for groups of unknown frequency. 0.1 (0.02-0.3).

rows.label: Years the connection effect lasts
rows.explainer: While people keep coming, plus a little; the yearly count is a yearly flow. Half a year (3 months to a year), as the Salvation Army model's community programmes.

rows.label: WELLBYs per alumni-event participant
WELLBYs per peer-group member, on top
Yearly suicide rate of US veterans

source.title: US Department of Veterans Affairs (December 2024), VA releases annual Veteran suicide prevention report analyzing 2001-2022 data
source.quote: there were 6,407 suicides among Veterans in 2022

rows.explainer: Per person per year. The VA counted 6,407 veteran suicides in 2022 among about 18 million veterans, about 35 per 100,000, and 46.2 per 100,000 among service members who left in 2021; post-9/11 veterans are younger than veterans overall, whose rates are higher. 36 per 100,000 (30-47), as the mental health model.

rows.label: Relative fall in suicide risk while in a peer support group
rows.explainer: Social connectedness is one of the strongest correlates of lower suicide risk among veterans, but trials of peer support show no clear effect on suicide itself (the VA's peer support specialists' evaluations measure engagement and hopelessness). 5% (0-15%) while the group lasts.

rows.label: Suicides averted per peer-group member (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: WWP's 'connection saves lives': the rate × the fall × the months it lasts, discounted.

rows.label: Participants in the 90-day coaching programme

source.title: Wounded Warrior Project, Form 990 for the year ended 30 September 2025
source.quote: OF THOSE PARTICIPANTS, 1,606 PARTICIPATED IN THE COACHING PROGRAM AND 74% SHOWED IMPROVED MOBILITY AFTER PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM.

rows.explainer: A 90-day programme of exercise, nutrition and sleep coaching with staff.

rows.label: Effect of coaching on wellbeing and depression measures (SD)
rows.explainer: Exercise reduces depressive symptoms by about 0.6 SD in people with depression in trials (Schuch et al. 2016, Journal of Psychiatric Research 77:42), much less in mixed groups and as quality of life; many of WWP's warriors have chronic pain (95% report pain in the past three months), where exercise programmes give small gains. 0.15 SD (0.03-0.4) for a 90-day programme without a control group of its own.

rows.label: Years the coaching effect lasts
rows.explainer: Exercise habits fade after a programme ends; follow-ups of exercise trials show partial maintenance at six to twelve months. 0.75 years (3 months to 2 years).

rows.label: WELLBYs per person coached
rows.explainer: The effect for its years, at the site's WELLBYs per SD-year, discounted.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained by other participants (events, rides, adaptive sports; points)
rows.explainer: A day or a few days of exercise with other veterans: a short lift, like the connection events (0.03) but more often a single day. 0.02 (0.005-0.08).

rows.label: Years the lift from an event lasts
rows.explainer: A day or a few days of exercise with other veterans: weeks to months. A quarter of a year (a few weeks to half a year).

rows.label: WELLBYs per other participant
rows.explainer: The lift for its months, discounted.

rows.explainer: In-home care and therapy are worth roughly their price to a household that needs them (care it would otherwise buy), less for alternative therapies (art, music, equine) the household wouldn't buy at that price. 0.7 (0.4-1). rows.explainer: Most of these warriors receive 100% VA disability compensation (over $45,000 a year) and Social Security disability; their spouses often can't work. About the benefits branch's 0.8 (0.5-1.1).

Not in the money value above, which counts the services to the household as a whole; a caregiver's relief from care that would otherwise be unpaid is the part money doesn't capture.

rows.label: Combat-injured veterans the Major Richard Star Act would pay

source.title: Wounded Warrior Project, 2025 Annual Report (fiscal year October 2024 to September 2025)
source.quote: the Major Richard Star Act, which would ensure nearly 54,000 combat-injured veterans receive the full retirement pay and disability benefits they have earned.

rows.explainer: WWP's top advocacy priority: Chapter 61 retirees with combat-related disabilities and under 20 years of service, whose retirement pay is now cut by their VA compensation. WWP's figure is 54,000; MOAA's September 2026 letter says 'nearly 59,000'. CBO's $13 billion prices this combat-injured group; 54,000 keeps the payment per veteran conservative within the 54,000-59,000 spread.

source.quote: Doing so would cost $13 billion over 10 years, according to the CBO estimate.

rows.explainer: CBO's estimate for the original scope (the combat-injured); the 2025 bill as drafted would also cover about 255,000 other medically retired veterans at $78 billion, a scope WWP's 54,000 doesn't count. Taken as the narrower bill WWP describes.

rows.label: Chance the Star Act becomes law by the end of the 120th Congress (January 2029)
rows.explainer: The window fiscal 2025's work can influence: the rest of the 119th Congress and the 120th. MOAA's September 2026 letter to the defence bill's conferees says the Act 'was absent from both the House and Senate versions of the NDAA', and it has failed in every Congress since 2017 despite majorities of both chambers as cosponsors, held back by its cost (CBO's estimate rose with the 2025 draft's wider scope). One event, drawn as happens or doesn't. 0.08 (0.02-0.25).

source.title: Military Officers Association of America (September 2026), letter to the FY2027 NDAA conferees
source.quote: was absent from both the House and Senate versions of the NDAA

rows.label: Share of that chance due to veterans' groups' advocacy at all
rows.explainer: A bill with this many cosponsors exists because of the groups' pressure, but passing depends on budget deals and leadership. Research on lobbying finds most campaigns change nothing in a given Congress (Baumgartner et al. 2009, Lobbying and Policy Change); organised constituent contact moved legislators' support by about 12 points in a field experiment (Bergan and Cole 2015). 0.5 (0.2-0.8).

rows.label: WWP's fiscal-2025 share of the coalition's resources on the Act over that window
rows.explainer: WWP leads the Star Act Alliance of more than 20 organisations (annual report p. 18), including MOAA, the VFW, the American Legion and DAV, several with larger lobbying staffs: perhaps 15% of the coalition's effort in a year. The window runs about four years (2025-2028), so one year of WWP's work is about a quarter of that: 0.04 (0.01-0.1). Each year's spending then claims only its own share of the chance.

rows.label: Years a won law counts
rows.explainer: The site's one number of years a won reform counts (docs/normalization.md 2.9).

rows.label: Years from passage until the payments start
rows.explainer: Laws on military retirement pay usually take effect at the start of the next fiscal year or later; the 2004 concurrent-receipt law phased in over ten years. 1.5 years (0.5-3).

rows.label: Value of WWP's other advocacy, as a multiple of the Star Act's
rows.explainer: The rest of the agenda as a multiple of the Star Act's expected value. Its largest money item, the Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act signed in January 2025, after the window's start (home care caps lifted, an assisted-living pilot), was scored by CBO at a few billion dollars over ten years, well under the Star Act's $13 billion, and WWP was one of dozens of groups behind it; mental health, brain injury, toxic exposure and women veterans add bills with smaller money effects. 0.5 (0.2-1.5).

rows.label: Years a gift waits before it is spent
rows.explainer: WWP held $182.5M of undesignated net assets at 30 September 2025 (audited statement of financial position, p. 3) against $390.3M of yearly spending: about half a year. The board also holds a $219.4M strategic fund and a $103.0M risk reserve (and $191.2M in the Long Term Support Trust), which a new gift may join instead: up to 1.8 years if all net assets count.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway, benefits service
rows.explainer: Free VA-accredited representation is everywhere: DAV, the VFW, the American Legion and county veteran service officers file most claims, and veterans can file alone. WWP reports an 83% approval rate on its claims in fiscal 2024 (87% in fiscal 2022, impact reports), against the VA's 64.6% grant rate for claims decided in fiscal 2024 to July, but much of that gap is which claims a representative takes on and who seeks help. WWP's help changes the award, or its timing (counted in ben_income_years), for perhaps 40% of its awards (20-70%).

Benefits service: the taxpayers' cost, units of value (adjusted, negative)
rows.formula: 0 - ben_economic_impact / ben_years_in_figure * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, ben_income_years) * taxpayer_ln_loss_per_dollar * $uov_per_ln_consumption * ben_total_adj
rows.explainer: The same dollars over the same years, at the marginal cost of public funds, spread over taxpayers: a transfer counts only by moving money from richer payers to poorer veterans (as habitat-for-humanity-charityevals-awareness counts public money).

rows.label: Months other claimants' awards are delayed per claim WWP's help adds
rows.explainer: Each claim added to the VA's queue delays others slightly; the VA's backlog of claims over 125 days varied between about 100,000 and 400,000 in 2022-2025 with its workload. A claim that wouldn't otherwise have been filed adds about a day of work for the system's claims staff; spread over the queue, it delays one other award by roughly 0.3 months (0-1.5).

rows.label: Benefits service: delay to other claimants, units of value (adjusted, negative)
rows.formula: 0 - ben_economic_impact / ben_years_in_figure * ben_queue_delay_months / 12 * ben_delay_loss_share / ben_baseline_consumption * $uov_per_ln_consumption * ben_total_adj
rows.explainer: Other veterans wait longer for awards of the same size: the months of delay × a month of an award, on the veterans' log scale. Delay only (back pay is paid later), so a share of it is a pure timing loss (ben_delay_loss_share).

rows.label: Share of a delayed award that is lost to the veteran (not repaid as back pay)
rows.explainer: Back pay restores the money but not its use when needed: the cost of waiting is borrowing, arrears and missed spending, about 0.3 of the month's value (0.1-0.6).
